info.description:
Complete API collection for Tazama Model Management Backend.

## Authentication
All requests require a Bearer token obtained from your authentication provider (Keycloak).

## Required Claims
- **GET operations**: `view-profile`, `editor`, `approver`, or `publisher`
- **POST/CREATE operations**: `editor`

## Base URL
Update the `{{baseUrl}}` variable with your Model-management backend URL (default: `http://localhost:3000`)

request.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of rules with optional filters.

### Query Parameters
- **offset**: Starting position (0-based index)
- **limit**: Number of records per page

### Request Body (Optional Filters)
You can filter results by any rule field:
- `status`: Filter by rule status (e.g., "ACTIVE", "INACTIVE", "DRAFT")
- `txtp`: Filter by transaction type (e.g., "pain.001.001.11")
- `publishing_status`: Filter by publishing status
- `rule_id`: Search by rule ID
- `rule_name`: Search by rule name

### Response
Returns an array of rule objects matching the filters.

### Required Claims
`editor`, `approver`, or `publisher`

request.description:
Retrieves a specific rule by its numeric ID.

### Path Parameters
- **id**: Numeric rule ID (integer)

### Response
Returns a single rule object with all fields:
- `rule_id`: Unique rule identifier
- `rule_name`: Human-readable rule name
- `description`: Rule description
- `tenant_id`: Tenant identifier
- `txtp`: Transaction type
- `version`: Rule version
- `status`: Rule status
- `publishing_status`: Publishing workflow status
- `updated_by`: Last user who modified the rule
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp

### Required Claims
`editor`, `approver`, or `publisher`

### Error Responses
- **400**: Invalid ID format (must be numeric)
- **404**: Rule not found

Creates a new rule for detecting high-value payment fraud.

### Request Body (Required Fields)
- **rule_id**: Unique identifier for the rule (alphanumeric with hyphens)
- **rule_name**: Human-readable name
- **description**: Detailed description of what the rule does
- **txtp**: Transaction type (e.g., "pain.001.001.11" for credit transfer)
- **version**: Semantic version (e.g., "1.0.0")
- **rule_type**: Type classification of the rule (e.g., "fraud_detection", "aml", "security", "compliance")

### Optional Fields
- **rule_config_id**: Configuration identifier for the rule (VARCHAR(10)) - links rule to its configuration
- **status**: Rule status - `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, `TESTING`
- **publishing_status**: Workflow status - `DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`, `PUBLISHED`

### Auto-populated Fields
The following fields are automatically set by the system with default values:
- **status**: Defaults to `ACTIVE` if not provided
- **publishing_status**: Defaults to `STATUS_01_IN_PROGRESS` if not provided
- **tenant_id**: Extracted from authentication token
- **updated_by**: User ID from authentication token
- **updated_at**: Current timestamp
- **created_at**: Current timestamp

### Required Claims
`editor`

### Response
Returns the created rule object with all fields populated (201 Created).

### Use Case
This rule monitors payment transfers (pain.001.001.11) for fraud patterns like:
- Transaction amounts exceeding $10,000
- Multiple high-value transactions within 5 minutes
- Transactions to flagged accounts

request.description:
Updates an existing rule with partial field updates. Only the fields provided in the request body will be modified; all other fields remain unchanged.

### Overview
This endpoint performs a partial update on a rule in the `trs_rules` table. You can update any subset of modifiable fields without affecting the rest of the rule data. This is useful for making targeted changes without needing to send the complete rule object.

### Path Parameters
- **ruleId**: The unique identifier of the rule to update (e.g., "RULE-001-PAYMENT-FRAUD")

### Request Body (All Fields Optional)
You can include any combination of the following fields:
- **rule_name**: Updated human-readable name
- **description**: Updated description
- **txtp**: Transaction type (e.g., "pain.001.001.11")
- **version**: Updated version number
- **status**: Updated status - `ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, `TESTING`, `DRAFT`
- **publishing_status**: Updated publishing workflow status - `DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`, `PUBLISHED`, `STATUS_04_APPROVED`, `STATUS_06_EXPORTED`
- **rule_type**: Type classification of the rule
- **rule_config_id**: Configuration identifier for the rule (VARCHAR(10))

### Auto-updated Fields
The following fields are automatically managed by the system:
- **updated_by**: Extracted from JWT token (user ID or client ID)
- **updated_at**: Set to current timestamp (NOW())
- **tenant_id**: Cannot be changed (preserved from original)
- **rule_id**: Cannot be changed (used as identifier)
- **created_at**: Cannot be changed (preserved from original)

### Required Claims
`editor` - Only users with editor privileges can update rules

request.description:
Updates the status of a specific rule identified by its rule ID.

### Overview
This endpoint allows you to change the status of a rule without modifying other rule properties. This is useful for quickly activating, deactivating, or changing the operational state of a rule.

### Path Parameters
- **ruleId**: The unique identifier of the rule to update (e.g., "RULE-001-PAYMENT-FRAUD")

### Request Body (Required)
- **status**: The new status value for the rule. Common values include:
  - `ACTIVE`: Rule is active and will be evaluated
  - `INACTIVE`: Rule is inactive and will not be evaluated
  - `TESTING`: Rule is in testing mode
  - `DRAFT`: Rule is in draft state

### Auto-updated Fields
The following fields are automatically managed by the system:
- **updated_by**: Extracted from JWT token (user ID or client ID)
- **updated_at**: Set to current timestamp

### Response
Returns the updated rule object with all fields, including the new status.

### Required Claims
`editor` - Only users with editor privileges can update rule status

### Use Cases
- Quickly enable or disable rules without full update
- Change rule operational state during maintenance
- Activate rules after testing
- Deactivate problematic rules immediately

### Error Responses
- **400**: Invalid request body or missing status field
- **404**: Rule not found
- **401**: Missing or invalid JWT token
- **403**: Insufficient permissions (requires editor claim)

request.description:
Retrieves all distinct transaction types from the `config` table.

### Overview
This endpoint fetches a unique list of all transaction types (txtp) configured in the system. Transaction types define the ISO 20022 message format for financial transactions, such as `pain.001.001.11` for credit transfers or `pacs.008.001.10` for payment clearing.

### Required Claims
`editor`, `approver`, or `publisher`

Retrieves all available versions for a specific transaction type.

### Overview
This endpoint fetches a list of all versions available for a given transaction type from the `config` table. This is useful for understanding version evolution and selecting appropriate configurations for different message versions.

### Path Parameters
- **transactionType**: ISO 20022 transaction type (e.g., "pain.001.001.11")

### Response
Returns an array of version strings for the specified transaction type.

```json
[
  "1.0.0",
  "1.1.0",
  "2.0.0"
]
```

### Required Claims
`editor`, `approver`, or `publisher`

### Use Cases
- Version management and tracking
- Configuration selection based on version
- API versioning support
- Backward compatibility verification

### Error Responses
- **400**: Invalid transaction type format
- **404**: No versions found for the specified transaction type
- **401**: Missing or invalid JWT token
- **403**: Insufficient permissions

request.description:
Processes a transactional message (pain.001, pacs.002, etc.) and logs it for analysis.

### Overview
This endpoint accepts ISO 20022 transactional messages for parsing and extraction. Currently, it logs the message details to the console for monitoring and debugging purposes. This is the foundation for future message parsing and data extraction functionality.

### Request Body
- **messageType**: Type of the transactional message (e.g., "pain.001", "pacs.002")
- **messageContent**: The actual message content (XML, JSON, or other formats)
- **messageId**: Unique identifier for the message (optional)
- **timestamp**: Message timestamp (optional, ISO 8601 format)
- **metadata**: Additional metadata about the message (optional)

### Response
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Successfully processed pain.001 message",
  "processedAt": "2026-01-05T10:30:15.123Z",
  "messageType": "pain.001",
  "messageId": "MSG-12345"
}
```

### Supported Message Types
- **pain.001**: Customer Credit Transfer Initiation
- **pain.002**: Customer Payment Status Report
- **pacs.002**: FI to FI Payment Status Report
- **pacs.008**: FI to FI Customer Credit Transfer
- **camt.054**: Bank to Customer Debit Credit Notification
- And other ISO 20022 message types

### Use Cases
- **Message Validation**: Verify message format and structure
- **Data Extraction**: Extract key fields from transactional messages
- **Audit Logging**: Log all incoming messages for compliance
- **Pre-processing**: Prepare messages for rule evaluation
- **Debugging**: Monitor message flow through the system

### Required Claims
`editor`, `approver`, or `publisher`

### Logging Output
The service logs the following information:
- Message type and ID
- Message timestamp
- Content preview (first 500 characters)
- Metadata (if provided)
- Processing status and completion time

### Future Enhancements
- Message parsing and field extraction
- Schema validation
- Message transformation
- Integration with rule evaluation engine
- Real-time message streaming

### Error Responses
- **400 Bad Request**: Invalid message format
- **401 Unauthorized**: Missing or invalid JWT token
- **403 Forbidden**: Insufficient permissions
- **500 Internal Server Error**: Processing failure

request.description:
Test processing of a large transactional message to verify content preview functionality.

### Purpose
This request tests the service's ability to handle large messages and demonstrates the content preview feature that truncates message content to the first 500 characters in the logs.

### Test Scenarios
- Large XML content processing
- Content preview truncation
- Metadata logging for batch operations
- Bulk transaction handling

### Expected Behavior
- Message content should be truncated in logs with "..." suffix
- All metadata should be logged completely
- Processing should succeed despite large content size
- Response should maintain the same structure as smaller messages
